title: Branch equations of an SNC boundary on a regular affine chart are nonzerodivisors
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring such that $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in A$, $r\geq0$, be equations of the pairwise distinct reduced irreducible branches of a strict normal crossings boundary on $X$, these branches being precisely the closed subschemes $V(t_d)$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Then for every $d$ multiplication by $t_d$ is injective on $A$; consequently multiplication by the product $t_1\cdots t_r$ is injective on $A$. The zero ring is permitted, and for $r=0$ the product is $1$.

source.place: Reviewer extraction of the returned normal-chart proof, Step 6 (codimension argument): definition-strict-normal-crossings (Tag 0BI9) with its codimension-one branches, algebra.tex lemma-regular-domain (Tag 00NP, regular local rings are domains) and lemma-characterize-zero-local (Tag 00HN, elements vanishing at all maximal localizations are zero). The combined assertion is derived, not verbatim.

proof.text: By the branch-support equality, each V(t_i) is the image in X of an irreducible component of the subtype |H|, hence V(t_i) is contained in |H|. The effective Cartier clause of [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] gives, near every point x, an affine open U on which H is generated by a nonzerodivisor g.

source.place: definition-strict-normal-crossings (0BI9), effective Cartier hypothesis; divisors.tex definition-effective-Cartier-divisor and lemma-characterize-effective-Cartier-divisor.

proof.text: Write s for the restriction to U of the global section corresponding to t_i. The support containment gives V(s) subset V(g). By the vanishing-ideal/radical correspondence, g belongs to the radical of (s), so g^n = c*s for some n and c. Powers of a nonzerodivisor are nonzerodivisors, and a factor of a nonzerodivisor is a nonzerodivisor: if s*a=s*b, multiply by c and cancel g^n. Thus multiplication by s is injective on every such U.

source.place: Elementary ideal radical criterion and cancellation; implemented by PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_subset_zeroLocus_singleton_iff, Ideal.mem_radical_iff, Ideal.mem_span_singleton', and mul_mem_nonZeroDivisors in Mathlib.

proof.text: If t_i*a=t_i*b, restriction to each Cartier chart gives equality of a and b there by Step 2. The sheaf separatedness axiom combines equality on a neighbourhood of each point to give equality of global sections. Transfer through the canonical isomorphism A = Gamma(Spec A,O) to obtain a=b in A. Products of nonzerodivisors are nonzerodivisors, including the empty product 1. This also covers the zero ring since all section and cancellation statements allow subsingleton rings.

Step 1: R=A_p≅O_{X,p} by spec-domain-stalks(1), which holds for any ring. R is regular local, a domain by lem-sc-regular-local-domain, and finite-dimensional because the Noetherian generator bound applies to m. Step 2: if t∉p then t/1 is a unit. Step 3: if t∈p then O_{C,p̄}≅R/tR, by localization-at-prime-of-quotient with I=(t). The singleton-J clause of def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary gives dim R=dim R/tR+1, so t/1=0 would give dim R=dim R+1, which is impossible, and cancellation in the domain R follows. Step 4: jointly-injective prime localizations give injectivity on A without assuming A is a domain. Step 5: induction on r, with r=0 and A=0 trivial. Tested cases: A=0, a DVR, k[x,y], k[x]×k with (x,1) (holds) and (x,0), which the SNC clause correctly excludes.
